source.display_title: 05/07/2026 - Omar Rosado x Farooq Bey  — Follow Up

prospect.name: Omar Rosado
prospect.aka: Rep addresses him once as 'Omo'; email captured on the recording as 'kdelso at gmo.com', which does not obviously correspond and is likely a transcription error
prospect.location: Stationed in Kansas, USA (Central time); originally from Puerto Rico
prospect.occupation: United States Army — describes his job as moving around and talking to people, high daily step count
prospect.family_status: Newly married; wife not named. Has a younger brother, a mother and a stepfather, none of whom exercise. Thinks in Spanish and translates to English.
prospect.training_background: Dislikes conventional gym machine work. Trains calisthenics — pull-ups, pike push-ups, deadlifts — plus running, sprinting and shadowboxing. Learned a handstand. Passes the Army physical test every six months (deadlift, push-up, plank, run). Tested with a good VO2 max result. No kettlebell experience, and believes kettlebells are dangerous. Previously paid roughly $1,000 to an online coach who did not respond to his questions.

signals: Proposed label: the_young_aspirant — early-career, low discretionary income, no prior decline to reverse, buying to build a foundation rather than to recover one. Recommend clustering centrally; nothing in the current vocabulary fits.

Not a rebuilder: he has lost no ground and names no former self. 'I stopped doing bad things when I wanted to join the army... What I have now is the little things that I started doing to make myself better.'
Not an optimizer: no income, no discretionary spend, $800 in the bank and a $200 credit limit

Motivation is anticipatory and biological — 'I'm 23, so this is the point of my life where I can make those neural connections for my muscles to actually be strong and stay strong. Because then, when I'm old, it's going to be hard to do it.'
Driver is family role-modelling rather than self-image: wants to be 'an image' to his younger brother and his wife, and worries his mother and stepfather will age badly
Trust is the live variable, not price appetite — he has been burned once already by a $1,000 online coach who ghosted him

goals.text: Become genuinely strong rather than 'not strong-strong' — able and capable, with a functional body
Build neural and strength adaptations now at 23 so they persist into old age
Get back to around 150 lb lean from 160 lb with added belly fat
Train in an old-school, non-machine way that he actually enjoys and will stick to
Acquire structured knowledge he can apply anywhere without needing a gym
Be an image and example to his younger brother so he takes care of himself
Be an example to his wife and teach her what he learns
Pass knowledge to his mother and stepfather so they do not age badly
Pass military fitness tests more comfortably

pains.text: Actively dislikes gym machine work and has avoided structured training because of it
Calisthenics and running are not producing change because he cannot load enough weight
No structure or path — 'I don't know where to go or how to do to be okay'
Previously paid around $1,000 to a coach who never answered his questions
Gaining weight despite eating what he considers a healthy, repetitive diet of rice, avocado and chicken
Believes kettlebell training is dangerous and has discouraged his wife from trying it
Newly married with roughly $2,600 monthly income, paying off his wife's car and setting up a household; around $800 in the bank and a $200 credit limit
Feels responsibility not to spend household money — 'I can't be a husband who can't provide'
Watched people at home in Puerto Rico not take care of themselves and does not want that for his family

objections.raw_quote: all of the money that I got, I only got a thousand dollars in my bank account right now that I can't stay without it because I can't be a husband who can't provide, you know?
objections.rep_response: Thanked him for honesty, isolated the money ('money aside, there's nothing else that's stopping you from really doing this'), then ran a partial financial picture — monthly surplus, credit score, credit card limit.

objections.raw_quote: Obviously, I need to talk all of this with her, man, because now we're a team. It sounds good, but she wants to do it, and from what I learned, I want to teach her, I guess, man.
objections.rep_response: Ran the full objection B play — asked whether she knows about the call, why she would want him stronger, what obstacles might come up, and who is responsible for the decision. Then asserted that in 2,000 conversations nobody who left to consult a spouse has ever come back, pressed him on whether he would proceed even against her refusal, and finally offered a $100 deposit with a refund promise.

objections.raw_quote: I think for her, the thing that puts it, and obviously for me, but I'm a little, I can trust, but she would be like, eh, like, but is it going to work? Like, is it something that good to invest on it?
objections.rep_response: Agreed the concern was reasonable — 'there's a lot of people who sell dreams out there' — then asked 'how would you know that this is going to work or not if you don't actually try it?'

objections.raw_quote: You're good, though, but I'm going come back to you.
objections.rep_response: Offered a small deposit of $100 or $200 to hold the commitment and rebook, framed as committing to what he had said on the call.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Three months spread over twelve months at 'like 430 bucks a month', later restated as '433', with the option to settle early. After the $100 deposit the rep restated the three-month total as $3,900 and said that could also be divided over twelve. Neither $430 x 12 ($5,160) nor $433 x 12 ($5,196) reconciles with a $4,000 or $3,900 total, and no financing cost was disclosed.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Given verbally and relied upon: 'if after that you say, she says, or you both say, hey, man, I can't, like, we hate this, then we can refund you.' No window, conditions or written terms were stated. The prospect explicitly conditioned his decision on it — 'if it's true what you say about the refund, I can make her trust me in that way, too.'

evidence: No programme tier was purchased. Only a $100 holding deposit was taken: 'if you want to speak later and you want to do this, we just take a small deposit. I don't care what it is, $100, $200. Then we can book you in the calendar again so we can get you onboarded.'
The prospect asked to reduce even that: 'you're happy with the $200 deposit? Can I do $100?'
Decision was explicitly deferred pending his wife: 'I'm going come back to you' and 'I'm new to the marriage, so I just want to make the option'
A follow-up call was booked for the next day at 5pm Central and a calendar email was confirmed received
Counter-evidence: the $100 payment was completed and confirmed on the record — 'We got it, bro. We got it. You've paid it. We've confirmed it.'
Counter-evidence: strong verbal intent — 'I'll be honest with you, man. I'm all in it. I want to do this', and when asked whether he would proceed against his wife's refusal he answered 'Probably'
Counter-evidence: he stated a preference for the three-month tier and understood the upgrade credit toward six months
Recorded as follow_up rather than closed because a $100 deposit against a $3,900-$4,000 programme is a hold, not a purchase, and the rep himself framed the next call as where onboarding would happen
outcome.cash_collection_basis: Holding deposit only — programme not purchased, no tier processed. Must not be counted as a programme sale or contract value in close-rate or cash rollups.
outcome.next_step: Rebooked call with the rep for the following day at 5pm Central time, wife invited to attend. Prospect to discuss with his wife in the interim. No Trevor onboarding call was scheduled.

notable.note: A 23-year-old junior soldier on roughly $2,600 a month, newly married, with about $800 in the bank and a $200 credit limit, was taken through the full spouse-consultation play and told 'when anyone says they speak to their wife, I've never seen anyone come back', then asked directly 'even if she says like, hell no, you're still going to do it?' — answer 'Probably.' A $100 deposit was taken on a refund promise the prospect explicitly said he would use to persuade his wife. Separately, the twelve-month payment structure quoted ($430-433 per month) implies roughly $5,160-5,196 against a stated price of $3,900-4,000, with no financing cost disclosed, and it contradicts the 'three months tops' in-house payment policy this rep stated on another call the previous day. The rep also moved receipt collection to his personal WhatsApp line.

quality.notes: Heavy inversion throughout, including the opening — 'Where are you calling from, Omar?' is attributed to Omar. The passage from 00:23:50 to 00:25:11 collapses roughly six alternating turns into a single unbroken block under one label, containing both the rep's three/six-month upsell explanation and the prospect's responses; it was untangled from content. There is a timestamp gap between 00:43:37 and 00:45:04 covering the receipt exchange. Roles resolved from content: Farooq Bey runs the call.
